title: Evelyn Knight and Carmen McRae
summary: He recalls Evelyn Knight, who wanted plain accompaniment before the show and jazz after, and Carmen.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: But to get back to the singers... I played for so many singers, I can't even tell you... One of the finest, one of the best singers I ever played for wasn't a Jazz singer. That's the funny part of it. Evelyn Knight. She was a socialite type. She worked at the Palmer House, and this and that, you know... Boy, what a woman! She was something else. I loved that girl! And she sang songs like "Grandfather's Clock" and "A Little Bird Told Me That You..." -- and she didn't want me to do nothin' but just OMM-CHI, OOM-CHI, OOM-CHI. An occasional Count Basie; I could get away with that, that was all right. But if I started playing funny chords, whoa, she'd call me down. Otherwise, everything was completely together.
She had guys chasing her... She was a beautiful girl!

She had guys like Milt Raskin, or Milt...the guy that bought RKO, Milt Raxson(?) or whatever his name is... Kind of like that. Millionaires! Called her from all over the world, all the time: "Evelyn, please marry me. Marry me. Marry me." Then I'd knock on the door, and she'd say...hang up, and say, "Wait a minute. What do you want? Money? How much do you want?" She'd write me out a check. Then she'd say, "Now, watch. Don't play them funny chords behind me. They go after the show."
And then after the show, she'd sing Jazz! She'd sing "No More..." She's the only girl I ever played for that sang "No More," outside of Lady Day. Evelyn Knight. And I adored her. I loved her...!
Same for Carmen. She'd come out there and give you a bad time... Sings real great. But the personality part, forget it. She and I are friends, you know, but not close.
